title: Marginalia
oneLiner: Ask a hosted reader a question about a PDF corpus and get claims whose quotes are verbatim, highlighted on the page, with an inspectable retrieval trace and a calibrated refusal.

live.firstAction: Ask the seeded Sentence-BERT paper why SBERT is more efficient than a BERT cross-encoder.
limits: The free instance sleeps after 15 minutes idle and takes about a minute to wake.
The hosted corpus is five papers and 260 chunks; a question outside it is refused.
A warm answer takes 17–25 s on the free instance.
A visitor upload is capped at 25 MB and 80 pages, sent to a third-party free-tier model, and deleted after 24 hours.

previewCommand: uv run docqa serve --port 8788  # then, in a second shell: npm --prefix ui run dev

invariants.claim: Ingest refuses a chunk longer than 448 model tokens rather than storing a truncated vector.
A claim without an in-context citation, or whose quote is not a normalised substring of the cited chunk, is dropped.
The refusal threshold comes from eval/calibration.json at boot and is never hand-tuned.
Every rate carries a Wilson 95% interval and its denominator; the eval records the earliest stage that produced no answer for each question.
The judge model differs from the generator and is pinned by exact id; its reliability is recorded by the judge check.
ONNX work runs in a worker thread behind Semaphore(2).

limits: Citation precision and faithfulness are rule-based, rest on n=15, and reach down to 54.8%.
Calibration is fitted in-sample on the same 30 questions.
The eval set is 30 questions; the intervals are wide.
